description: What GET /api/redfish/v1/Systems/{sid} accepts and refuses on this device, and what the two actions answer, recorded by hand against kvmd 4.186 (see README). The capture tool only records GETs that succeed; these are the empty 204s and the refusals, which no capture had. kvmd also accepts every SwitchPort<N> a real switch exposes; this device has none, so no accepted port id is recorded here.
safety: The device records with atx.type = disabled, whose plugin returns a hardcoded enabled=false and whose every action raises AtxDisabledError. kvmd dispatches a reset of Systems/0 only when the ATX is enabled, so the accepted reset below performed no power action; the target machine's video stayed online across it. Note that the enabled check guards the Systems/0 branch only — a SwitchPort<N> reset acts on the port whatever atx.type is set to.

steps.name: system_zero
steps.note: the only numeric id kvmd knows: a legacy name for the machine PiKVM is wired to, and a string in the document it returns

steps.name: system_one
steps.note: the id aiopikvm's int-typed parameter made reachable; kvmd has never accepted it

steps.name: system_zero_padded
steps.note: compared as a string, so 00 is not 0

steps.name: switch_port_absent
steps.note: a well-formed switch port id on a device with no switch attached; the message differs from an unknown id, so the form itself was accepted

steps.name: patch_system
steps.note: a stub: 204, no body, the request body ignored, the id not even validated. A GET straight after returned the document unchanged

steps.name: reset_type_from_the_dmtf_schema
steps.note: GracefulRestart is valid Redfish and not one of the six kvmd implements; aiopikvm's own docs used to advertise it

steps.name: reset_type_wrong_case
steps.note: kvmd checks the list with lower=False

steps.name: reset_type_missing
steps.note: a body with no ResetType. An entirely absent body was sent too and refused identically, before any action is dispatched; only this one is recorded

steps.name: set_default_boot_order
steps.note: advertised in every system document's Actions block, and not implemented; the 404 is aiohttp's, so it is plain text rather than a kvmd envelope
